reasoning_traces.think:
The core principle of multi-camera systems lies in combining independent visual inputs to enhance perception fidelity. Calibration ensures geometric consistency across cameras, enabling accurate triangulation and depth estimation. In surveillance, this supports coordinated tracking; in sports, it enables multi-angle analysis; in education, it allows comprehensive monitoring; and in mobile devices, it improves photography. The failure mode occurs when calibration errors propagate, leading to misalignment or incorrect fusion. The mathematical framework relies on projective geometry and rigid body transformations. Each camera contributes a view defined by intrinsic and extrinsic parameters. Fusion strategies include max pooling, weighted averaging, or deep learning-based aggregation. The system's robustness depends on minimizing reprojection error and maintaining temporal coherence. Dualities emerge in how spatial redundancy translates to temporal stability—both are essential for real-time inference in GSI and situational awareness in GSE.
